content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn to body surf, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Watch a documentary on ocean safety (1 hour)
Step 2. Research the best local beaches for beginners (30 minutes)
Step 3. Practice holding your breath in a swimming pool (2 minutes)
Step 4. Buy a pair of high-quality swim fins (45 minutes)
Step 5. Apply waterproof sunscreen to your back (5 minutes)
Step 6. Practice the "streamline" body position on dry land (10 minutes)
Step 7. Check the local tide charts for the day (5 minutes)
Step 8. Pack a gear bag with towels and water (10 minutes)
Step 9. Stretch your hamstrings and lower back (15 minutes)
Step 10. Do twenty push-ups to warm up your arms (2 minutes)
Step 11. Put on a protective rash guard (3 minutes)
Step 12. Drive to the selected beach (45 minutes)
Step 13. Eat a light, energy-rich snack (15 minutes)
Step 14. Watch the wave sets from the shore for patterns (20 minutes)
Step 15. Tether your swim fins to your ankles (2 minutes)
Step 16. Practice kicking with fins in shallow water (15 minutes)
Step 17. Locate the lifeguard tower (5 minutes)
Step 18. Practice a deep breathing recovery cycle (5 minutes)
Step 19. Identify any visible rip currents (10 minutes)
Step 20. Wade out into the waist-deep water (5 minutes)
Step 21. Catch your first small broken wave (10 seconds)
Step 22. Introduce yourself to the local lifeguard (5 minutes)
Step 23. Read a book on hydrodynamics (3 days)
Step 24. Swim past the breaking surf line (8 minutes)
Step 25. Rinse your new fins to remove factory residue (2 minutes)
Step 26. Buy a parking pass for the coastal zone (10 minutes)
Step 27. Take an online course on wave mechanics (4 hours)
Step 28. Perform a series of jumping jacks on the sand (3 minutes)
Step 29. Check the wind direction and speed (5 minutes)
Step 30. Look up the water temperature (2 minutes)
Step 31. Walk from the parking lot to the sand (5 minutes)
Step 32. Secure your car keys in a waterproof pouch (2 minutes)
Step 33. Dive under an incoming wave to get wet (30 seconds)
Step 34. Check the surf report for swell height (5 minutes)
Step 35. Purchase a basic ocean safety handbook (15 minutes)
Step 36. Summarize the safety rules to a friend (10 minutes)
Step 37. Read the warning signs posted at the beach entrance (2 minutes)
Step 38. Fasten a silicon swim cap (1 minute)
Step 39. Perform a quick mental focus exercise (2 minutes)
Step 40. Position your body to face the shore (10 seconds)
